target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### tree_ok

``` python
def tree_ok(
    p, root, most:int=None
)->bool:
```

*Whether abhyasa may read the file `p` under the folder `root`: not a
link, not a hard link, at most `most` bytes (default `TREE_MB` MB), and
inside `root` after each link is resolved.*

A small folder: two notebooks, a note, a data folder, a `.git` folder, a
file of another type, and a link to a file outside the folder.

``` python
import tempfile
from collections import Counter
from fastcore.nbio import new_nb, mk_cell, write_nb
```

``` python
def two_notebooks(d):
    "Write `01_a.ipynb` and `02_b.ipynb` in the folder `d`."
    write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# Noise\n\nA diffusion model adds noise, then learns to remove it.', 'markdown'), mk_cell('x = 1')]), Path(d)/'01_a.ipynb')
    write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell('# Steps\n\nThe sampler removes the noise in small steps.', 'markdown')]), Path(d)/'02_b.ipynb')

top = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
d = top/'course'; (d/'data').mkdir(parents=True); (d/'.git').mkdir()
two_notebooks(d)
(d/'notes.md').write_text('# Notes\n\nThe UNet predicts the noise.')
(d/'data/big.txt').write_text('data'); (d/'.git/config.txt').write_text('git'); (d/'model.pkl').write_text('bytes')
(top/'secret.txt').write_text('outside'); (d/'link.txt').symlink_to(top/'secret.txt'); os.link(top/'secret.txt', d/'key.txt')
(d/'tool.py').write_text('print(1)')
```

[`tree_files`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#tree_files)
keeps the two notebooks and the note. It skips the data folder, the
`.git` folder, the `.pkl` file, the link, the hard link `key.txt` and,
since the folder has notebooks, `tool.py`.

``` python
test_eq([p.name for p in tree_files(d)], ['01_a.ipynb', '02_b.ipynb', 'notes.md'])
test_eq(tree_files(d).cut, '')
```

The caps: with a cap of 2 files, or of 1 MB in all,
[`tree_files`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#tree_files)
keeps the first files and says why it stopped. A file over `TREE_MB` is
never read.

``` python
was = TREE_FILES, TREE_MB, TREE_TOTAL_MB
TREE_FILES = 2
t = tree_files(d); test_eq((len(t), t.cut), (2, 'abhyasa stopped at 2 files.'))
TREE_FILES, TREE_TOTAL_MB = 400, 1
(d/'big.md').write_bytes(b'x' * (2**20 - 10))
t = tree_files(d); test_eq((t.cut, 'big.md' in [p.name for p in t]), ('abhyasa stopped at 1 MB.', False))
TREE_TOTAL_MB, TREE_MB = 200, 0.5
test_eq(('big.md' in [p.name for p in tree_files(d)], tree_files(d).cut), (False, ''))
TREE_FILES, TREE_MB, TREE_TOTAL_MB = was; (d/'big.md').unlink()
```

A temp tree with the shape of diffusers: a README, 30 examples with a
README and a training script each, 450 English docs, 50 Korean docs, 3
notebooks and 2,000 other `.py` files.

``` python
big = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()).resolve()/'diffusers'
def put(rel, s='x'): (big/rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); (big/rel).write_text(s)
put('README.md', '# Diffusers')
for k in ['text_to_image', 'dreambooth', *[f'ex{i:02d}' for i in range(28)]]: put(f'examples/{k}/README.md'); put(f'examples/{k}/train_{k}.py')
put('examples/text_to_image/train_text_to_image_lora.py')
for i in range(450): put(f'docs/source/en/page{i:03d}.md')
for i in range(50): put(f'docs/source/ko/page{i:03d}.md')
for i in range(3): write_nb(new_nb([mk_cell(f'# Notebook {i}', 'markdown')]), big/f'nb{i}.ipynb')
for i in range(2000): put(f'src/diffusers/m{i:04d}.py')
```

abhyasa files 400 files. The README, the notebooks, each README and
training script of `examples/` are in. `docs/` gives no more than its
cap and the room that is left, and no Korean page. `src/` gives the rest
of the room.

``` python
t = tree_files(big)
rel = [p.relative_to(big).as_posix() for p in t]
test_eq((len(t), t.cut), (TREE_FILES, f'abhyasa stopped at {TREE_FILES} files.'))
for x in ['README.md', 'nb0.ipynb', 'nb2.ipynb', 'examples/text_to_image/README.md', 'examples/dreambooth/README.md',
          'examples/text_to_image/train_text_to_image_lora.py', 'examples/ex27/train_ex27.py']: assert x in rel, x
by = Counter(r.split('/')[0] if '/' in r else '' for r in rel)
test_eq((by['examples'], by['src']), (61, TREE_TOP))
assert TREE_TOP <= by['docs'] < 450 and not any('/ko/' in r for r in rel)
```

A file that you name comes first. A course keeps its notebooks and no
other code, and a small code folder keeps all of its files.

``` python
assert 'src/diffusers/m1999.py' in [p.relative_to(big).as_posix() for p in tree_files(big, want=['src/diffusers/m1999.py'])]
test_eq((tree_rank('tool.py', course=True), tree_rank('examples/a/train_a.py', course=True), tree_rank('docs/source/en/x.md')), (None, 4, 6))
test_eq(tree_rank('docs/source/pt-BR/x.md'), 9)
```

### Which folders abhyasa files

[`folder_why`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#folder_why)
says why abhyasa does not file a folder, or gives `''`. The folder must
be a real folder in your home folder. It must not be the home folder
itself, a hidden folder (a name that starts with a dot) or a link. The
test folder is not in the home folder, so it is refused.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L723"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### folder_why

``` python
def folder_why(
    p
)->str:
```

*Why abhyasa does not file the folder `p` (the rules of
`settings.source_root_why`), or ’’ when it can. It must be a folder that
you can read.*

``` python
test_eq(folder_why(d), 'abhyasa reads only folders in your home folder.')
test_eq(folder_why('~'), 'Name a folder in your home folder, not the home folder itself.')
test_eq(folder_why('~/.ssh'), 'abhyasa does not read a hidden folder or a link.')
test_eq(folder_why('~/no-such-folder-for-abhyasa'), NO_FOLDER)
```

### Filing a folder

[`_file_tree`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#_file_tree)
files the files of a folder on a shelf. A notebook or a file with the
same mtime as its copy on the shelf is not read again. Each document
gets `meta.root`, `meta.path` and `meta.mtime`, and `meta.url` when
`url` gives one. The result has the shape of
[`file_link`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_link),
with `mtime`. Its `added` holds only the documents that were not on the
shelf before, so an Undo never forgets a document that you had before.

[`file_folder`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_folder)
checks the folder with
[`folder_why`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#folder_why)
first. It raises
[`LinkError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#linkerror)
with the plain reason. A document that was on the shelf before, filed by
another tool or by an older abhyasa, keeps its meta. `cut` says when a
cap stopped the filing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L752"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### file_folder

``` python
def file_folder(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, path, shelf:str='notebooks', want:tuple=()
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*File the folder `path` in your home folder on `shelf`. Each doc keeps
`meta.root` (the folder name) and `meta.path`. Raises
[`LinkError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#linkerror)
for a folder that abhyasa does not file.*

The test folder files three documents with `meta.root`. A second filing
reads nothing again and adds nothing.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
docs = _file_tree(lr, d, 'notebooks', 'course')
test_eq(len(docs), 3)
test_eq({lr.vault.shelf('notebooks').doc(x.doc_id)['meta']['root'] for x in docs}, {'course'})
test_eq(len(docs.added), 3)
again = _file_tree(lr, d, 'notebooks', 'course')
test_eq((again, len(again.added)), (docs, 0))
test_fail(lambda: file_folder(lr, d), contains='home folder')
```

### Undo

[`unfile`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#unfile)
forgets the documents of one filing. It forgets a document only when it
is still the same file: the same id and the same mtime. It gives the
count.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L773"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### unfile

``` python
def unfile(
    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, docs
)->int:
```

*Forget the docs that one filing added, when each is still the same file
(same id, same mtime). Returns the count.*

``` python
test_eq(unfile(lr, docs.added[:1]), 1)
test_eq(vault_roots(lr), {'course': 2})
test_eq(unfile(lr, docs.added[:1]), 0)   # it is gone already
```

### A GitHub repo

[`gh_name`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#gh_name)
reads `owner/name` from a GitHub link, or from the bare `owner/name`. A
pair of common words, such as `and/or`, is not a repo. A host that is
not github.com gives None.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L786"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### gh_name

``` python
def gh_name(
    s:str
)->str | None:
```

*`owner/name` of the GitHub repo that `s` names (a github.com link, or
`owner/name`), or None.*

``` python
test_eq(gh_name('fastai/diffusion-nbs'), 'fastai/diffusion-nbs')
test_eq(gh_name('https://github.com/fastai/diffusion-nbs.git'), 'fastai/diffusion-nbs')
test_eq(gh_name('github.com/fastai/course22/blob/master/README.md'), 'fastai/course22')
for s in ('and/or', '10/30', 'a/..', 'https://gitlab.com/a/b', '~/code/x', 'docs.python.org/3'): test_eq(gh_name(s), None)
```

[`file_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#file_repo)
clones only a public repo on github.com. It asks GitHub first
([`gh_public`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#gh_public)):
a private repo, a repo that is not there, or a repo bigger than
`REPO_MB` MB is refused. Then
[`clone_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#clone_repo)
gives the HTTPS link that was checked to fossick’s `gh_clone`, which
clones it into fossick’s cache folder. It uses HTTPS only, never SSH,
clones only the last commit (depth 1), puts `--` before the link, and
stops git after 600 seconds. It removes a clone that stopped half way,
and it changes no environment variable. abhyasa has no clone code of its
own. fossick is a core dependency, so no extra is necessary. A repo that
is in the cache already is brought up to date, not cloned again. The
research agent uses
[`clone_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#clone_repo)
too, so a repo is on the disk one time. Each document keeps
`meta.root='owner/name'` and `meta.url`, the GitHub page of the file.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L816"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### file_repo

``` python

    lr:abhyasa.store.Learning, url:str, shelf:str='notebooks', want:tuple=()
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Clone the public GitHub repo `url` (a link or `owner/name`) with
[`clone_repo`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#clone_repo),
then file it on `shelf`. Raises
[`LinkError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#linkerror)
with a plain reason.*

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L806"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python

    url:str, timeout:float=600
)->tuple:
```

*`(owner/name, folder)` for the public GitHub repo `url` (a link or
`owner/name`), cloned or brought up to date by fossick’s `gh_clone` in
its cache. Raises
[`LinkError`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#linkerror)
with a plain reason.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/sources.py#L796"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### gh_public

``` python
def gh_public(
    owner:str, name:str
)->dict | None:
```

*What GitHub says of the repo `owner/name` (`private`, `size` in KB), or
None when it has no such repo. With gheasy installed, its `gh_token`
gives a token, for more calls an hour.*

[`gh_public`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#gh_public)
sends a token from gheasy’s `gh_token` when gheasy is installed. GitHub
gives 60 calls an hour with no token. A bad token (401) gets one more
call with no token, and with no gheasy no token goes. A fake `http_get`
stands for GitHub.

``` python
import fossick, sys, types
```

``` python
sent = []
def fake_get(url, **kw):
    "GitHub: 401 for a bad token, else a public repo of 10 KB."
    sent.append((kw.get('headers') or {}).get('Authorization'))
    return AttrDict(status=401 if sent[-1] == 'Bearer bad' else 200, body=b'{"private": false, "size": 10}')
was_get, mods = fossick.http_get, {k: sys.modules.get(k) for k in ('gheasy', 'gheasy.core')}
def token(t): sys.modules['gheasy'] = sys.modules['gheasy.core'] = types.SimpleNamespace(gh_token=lambda: t)
fossick.http_get = fake_get
try:
    token('good'); test_eq(gh_public('a', 'b')['size'], 10); test_eq(sent, ['Bearer good'])
    sent.clear(); token('bad'); test_eq(gh_public('a', 'b')['size'], 10); test_eq(sent, ['Bearer bad', None])   # a bad token: one more call with none
    sent.clear(); sys.modules['gheasy'] = sys.modules['gheasy.core'] = None; gh_public('a', 'b'); test_eq(sent, [None])   # no gheasy: no token
finally:
    fossick.http_get = was_get
    for k, v in mods.items():
        if v is None: sys.modules.pop(k, None)
        else: sys.modules[k] = v
```

A test clone: a fake fossick `gh_clone` copies the test folder, and a
fake
[`gh_public`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#gh_public)
says that the repo is public. Nothing goes to the network.

``` python
import sys, types
```

``` python
cache = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
def fake_clone(url, timeout=None):
    "A clone with no network: it copies the test folder the first time, and keeps the link and the time limit that it got."
    got.append((url, timeout)); to = cache/url.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
    if not to.exists(): shutil.copytree(d, to)
    return to

got, real, real_clone = [], gh_public, fossick.gh_clone
fossick.gh_clone, gh_public = fake_clone, lambda o, n: dict(private=False, size=10)
try:
    lr = temp_learning()
    docs = file_repo(lr, 'https://github.com/fastai/course')
    m = lr.vault.shelf('notebooks').doc(docs[0].doc_id)['meta']
    test_eq((m['root'], m['url'], got), ('fastai/course', 'https://github.com/fastai/course/blob/HEAD/01_a.ipynb', [('https://github.com/fastai/course', 600)]))
    test_eq(file_repo(lr, 'fastai/course').attrgot('doc_id'), docs.attrgot('doc_id'))   # in the cache: the same documents
    gh_public = lambda o, n: dict(private=True); got.clear()
    test_fail(lambda: file_repo(lr, 'fastai/other'), contains='not a public repo'); test_eq(got, [])   # a private repo is never cloned
    gh_public = lambda o, n: dict(private=False, size=REPO_MB * 1024 + 1)
    test_fail(lambda: file_repo(lr, 'fastai/big'), contains='too big'); test_eq(got, [])
    test_fail(lambda: file_repo(lr, 'and/or'), contains='only a public repo')
finally: gh_public, fossick.gh_clone = real, real_clone
```

## The source of a passage

The source line uses `datetime` for the day that the tutor read a web
page.

[`source_of`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/detect.html#source_of)
gives the source line of a passage: one label, the title, a link to the
document, the place and the date. A passage from the web has the label
`from the web`. A passage from a document of yours has `your source`.
Text with no passage is the tutor’s own words. The walk, the talk and
the recap file all draw this one line.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/detect.py#L63"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### source_of

``` python
def source_of(
    read:dict, j:dict | None=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The source line of the passage `read` (a step `read`, a slide source or
a cite) in walk `j`: its
[`label`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/ground.html#label), its
`title`,* `href` (its document in the vault), `place` (the section and
the page, or the site of a web page), `url` (a web page) and `date`. The
place starts with `what`, the kind of text, when the passage has one
(such as `Summary`), so a summary never reads as a quote.

A passage of a paper in the vault names the paper, the section number
and the page, and links to the document.

``` python
p = source_of(dict(shelf='store', doc_id='d1', title='Attention Is All You Need', section='3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention', page=4, text='We suspect.'))
test_eq((p.label, p.title, p.href, p.place, p.url, p.date), ('your source', 'Attention Is All You Need', '/v/store/d1', 'section 3.2.1 · p. 4', '', ''))
```

A passage from the web names its site and the day it was read, and keeps
the link to the page.

``` python
w = source_of(dict(src='web', shelf='store', doc_id='d2', title='Softmax explained', site='example.org', url='https://example.org/s', text='Q.', at=datetime(2026, 10, 29, 12).timestamp()))
test_eq((w.label, w.href, w.place, w.url, w.date), ('from the web', '/v/store/d2', 'example.org', 'https://example.org/s', '29 Oct 2026'))
```

A cite on a vault shelf links to its document. A step with no passage is
the tutor’s words. A link that is not a web page is not kept.

``` python
test_eq(source_of(dict(src='vault:notes', ref='n1#2', title='My notes')).href, '/v/notes/n1')
test_eq(source_of(dict(src='vedicreader', ref='a:1', title='Ashtadhyayi 1 2')).place, 'vedicreader')
test_eq(source_of(dict(text=''), dict(source=dict(title='A paper'))).label, 'tutor')
test_eq(source_of(dict(src='web', url='javascript:alert(1)', text='Q.')).url, '')
```
